stages.note: The commands on this page are for a Linux or macOS terminal. On Windows, you run them in WSL2: a Linux system that Microsoft builds into Windows 10 (version 2004 or later) and Windows 11. On macOS or Linux, skip this stage.

steps.who: The agent opens an administrator PowerShell after your yes; Windows asks you to approve it (UAC)
steps.d: Check first (no change, no admin needed): Get-CimInstance Win32_OptionalFeature -Filter "Name='VirtualMachinePlatform'" and the same for Name='Microsoft-Windows-Subsystem-Linux' (InstallState 1 = enabled, 2 = disabled, 3 = absent). Check the Ubuntu distro too: no entries under HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Lxss means none installed. If both features are on, the feature step needs no restart: say so, and only the Ubuntu install is left. Only if a feature is off, after your yes, the agent starts an elevated PowerShell (Start-Process powershell -Verb RunAs) that runs the command and writes its output to a log file. You approve the Windows admin prompt on your screen. The install turns on the features WSL2 needs: they take effect after a restart, because Windows loads the WSL2 Linux kernel at boot. A failed install stops with the log's last lines; the agent does not retry in a loop. Restart only if a feature was off before the install, and only after you say yes; the agent saves the ledger first. After the restart, the agent checks again: if no Ubuntu with VERSION 2 is listed, it runs this install again after your yes.

After the install (and the restart, if one was needed), open Ubuntu from the Start menu once. The first start asks you to make a Linux user name and password; the agent cannot run commands in Ubuntu until you do this. Then say "done". Run every later command on this page in this Ubuntu window.
steps.c: sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y curl unzip jq openssl ca-certificates

steps.d: Click the link in the verification email soon after you get it. If the link has expired, sign in at multicloud.io and ask for a new email. If no email arrives, check your spam or quarantine folder, then tell your Multicloud contact.
You become the organization owner. Write down the organization ID: you may need it later.

stages.t: Install the tools and sign in to AWS
stages.note: You need four command-line tools. Your AI can install them for you, or you can run the commands below yourself.

steps.h: Optional: ask your AI to connect AWS
steps.d: Say: “Connect my AWS account to Multicloud. Use region us-east-1.” Your AI checks which tools are missing and guides you through this stage and the next one. The commands below are the same steps, if you prefer to run them yourself.
mctl needs Python 3.10 or later. The uv tool installs Python for you. Open a new terminal after the install.

os.mac:
brew install uv        # Homebrew: https://brew.sh
uv tool install multicloud-cli
uv tool update-shell
mctl --version
os.linux:
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
source "$HOME/.local/bin/env"
uv tool install multicloud-cli
uv tool update-shell
mctl --version
os.win:
# In the Ubuntu window
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
source "$HOME/.local/bin/env"
uv tool install multicloud-cli
uv tool update-shell
mctl --version

steps.d: The output of aws --version must start with aws-cli/2.

os.linux:
sudo apt install -y unzip        # or: sudo dnf install -y unzip
curl "https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-x86_64.zip" -o awscliv2.zip
unzip -q -o awscliv2.zip && sudo ./aws/install --update && rm -rf awscliv2.zip aws
aws --version
os.win:
# In the Ubuntu window
sudo apt install -y unzip        # or: sudo dnf install -y unzip
curl "https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-x86_64.zip" -o awscliv2.zip
unzip -q -o awscliv2.zip && sudo ./aws/install --update && rm -rf awscliv2.zip aws
aws --version

steps.g: ARM Linux (uname -m prints aarch64): use awscli-exe-linux-aarch64.zip.

steps.d: OpenTofu creates the Multicloud role in your AWS account. Terraform 1.10 or later also works.

os.linux:
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSL https://get.opentofu.org/install-opentofu.sh -o install-opentofu.sh
chmod +x install-opentofu.sh && ./install-opentofu.sh --install-method standalone
rm install-opentofu.sh && tofu version
os.win:
# In the Ubuntu window
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSL https://get.opentofu.org/install-opentofu.sh -o install-opentofu.sh
chmod +x install-opentofu.sh && ./install-opentofu.sh --install-method standalone
rm install-opentofu.sh && tofu version

steps.d: You need them from the stage “Prepare your cluster” on. The connector needs helm 3.14 or later.

os.mac:
brew install kubectl helm jq
kubectl version --client && helm version
os.linux:
curl -LO "https://dl.k8s.io/release/$(curl -Ls https://dl.k8s.io/release/stable.txt)/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl"
sudo install -m 0755 kubectl /usr/local/bin/kubectl && rm kubectl
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash
sudo apt install -y jq        # or: sudo dnf install -y jq
kubectl version --client && helm version
os.win:
# In the Ubuntu window
curl -LO "https://dl.k8s.io/release/$(curl -Ls https://dl.k8s.io/release/stable.txt)/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl"
sudo install -m 0755 kubectl /usr/local/bin/kubectl && rm kubectl
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash
sudo apt install -y jq
kubectl version --client && helm version

steps.g: ARM Linux (uname -m prints aarch64): replace linux/amd64 with linux/arm64 in the kubectl URL.
